prompt:
Two coplanar forces act on a post at the origin O:
- Force F1 has magnitude 50.0 N acting at an angle of 30.0 degrees above the positive x-axis (in quadrant 1).
- Force F2 has magnitude 40.0 N acting at an angle of 45.0 degrees above the negative x-axis (in quadrant 2).
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: Coordinate axes x and y. Origin O. Vector F1 = 50.0 N in the first quadrant at 30.0 degrees to the positive x-axis. Vector F2 = 40.0 N in the second quadrant at 45.0 degrees to the negative x-axis.]

(a)(i) Calculate the x-component and y-component of force F1. [1]
(a)(ii) Calculate the x-component and y-component of force F2, stating appropriate signs for your chosen axes. [1]
(b)(i) Calculate the components Rx and Ry of the resultant force R = F1 + F2. [1]
(b)(ii) Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force R. [1]
(b)(iii) Calculate the angle that the resultant force R makes with the positive x-axis. [1]
(c) Explain why resolving vectors into perpendicular components allows any number of coplanar vectors to be added accurately. [1]

answer.text:
(a)(i) F1x = 50.0 * cos(30.0 degrees) = +43.3 N; F1y = 50.0 * sin(30.0 degrees) = +25.0 N.
(a)(ii) F2x = -40.0 * cos(45.0 degrees) = -28.3 N; F2y = +40.0 * sin(45.0 degrees) = +28.3 N.
(b)(i) Rx = F1x + F2x = +43.3 - 28.3 = +15.0 N; Ry = F1y + F2y = +25.0 + 28.3 = +53.3 N.
(b)(ii) R = sqrt(Rx^2 + Ry^2) = sqrt(15.0^2 + 53.3^2) = sqrt(225 + 2840.9) = sqrt(3065.9) = 55.4 N.
(b)(iii) tan(phi) = Ry / Rx = 53.3 / 15.0 = 3.553, so phi = arctan(3.553) = 74.3 degrees above the positive x-axis.
(c) Perpendicular components along the x-axis and y-axis are independent of each other; components along the same axis can be added directly as algebraic scalar values, reducing any complex vector sum to two perpendicular resultant components.
